exitCriteria.title: Explore provides the four required modes and four reference-boundary overlays
exitCriteria.reason: Narrowed by owner scope decision on 2026-08-29, then met. The four modes render. Federal ridings, the BC, Alberta, Ontario and Quebec provincial ridings, the 44 Statistics Canada 2021 economic regions that lie in British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario and Quebec, and the 105 Canadian areas of NRCan's Water Survey of Canada version 6.0 rollup that intersect those four provinces, are drawn from one immutable v4 PMTiles release with exact remote readback and bilingual attribution. The economic-region and watershed layers were clipped to the four provinces on 2026-09-02, so both are now subsets: 44 of 76 regions, and 105 of the 169 Canadian sub-drainage areas, cut at the provincial boundary. An earlier revision of this reason still claimed all 76 regions and all 169 areas after the clip had shipped, because that change refreshed the bound checksums without rereading the sentence they support. Economic regions and watersheds are boundary-only reference frameworks, not forest-loss aggregates. The reserve and treaty-area overlays were removed from Explore, not delivered, and this criterion no longer stands in for them: that obligation is tracked solely by reserve-and-treaty-layers-loaded, which remains failed. If this criterion is ever read as evidence that reserve or treaty geography ships, it is being read wrongly. On 2026-09-19 the version in this reason was corrected from v3 to v4. lib/explore/boundaries.ts has pinned boundary-overlays-v4 release 594e33aa08fd7b60a21e6a17d43f7491757d99e7900fdd697230f6d1f52b78f0 since 2026-09-18, and the v4 record carries the same 44 economic regions and 105 watersheds clipped to the four provinces, and the same unclipped riding layers, that this reason describes. The sentence was wrong about the release it named, not about what ships. This is the second time this criterion has had a claim corrected after a checksum refresh changed the files under it without the sentence being reread. On 2026-09-20 ExploreView.tsx was moved into a three-column grid, controls left, map centre, figures right. The bound digest was refreshed for that move alone: the four modes and the four boundary overlays render exactly as this reason describes, placement is by named grid area so the document order is unchanged, and no release, clip, attribution or removal named above was touched. On 2026-09-21 tests/explore.test.tsx moved for the whole-area boundary pick; its four overlays and modes are unchanged. On 2026-09-23 ExploreView.tsx, explore.test.tsx changed for a plain-language wording pass alone; their digests were refreshed, and this reason still holds. On 2026-09-23 ExploreView.tsx and tests/explore.test.tsx changed for the owner-approved Explore layout: the four modes are a row of links above the map and the four boundary overlays sit in a Boundaries menu beside them, each with the same show and hide control, note and attribution. Their digests were refreshed, and this reason still holds.

exitCriteria.title: Explore uses native year selects whose keyboard interaction changes the selected span
exitCriteria.reason: Explore renders two native select elements with bounded years: the opening year runs from 1984 to 2021 and the closing year from 1985 to 2022. Because they are native selects, the browser supplies their keyboard interaction and their screen-reader announcements, and every change, however it is made, commits the new span to the address and the map. The focused route test pins both elements and their option ranges, and tests/browser/year-control.spec.ts changes the span with the keyboard alone. A choice that would reverse or empty the span moves the other select to the nearest valid year and says so in a status line, so the span is never zero-length. The annual interval is the narrowest span rather than a separate mode, so a link naming only its closing year still means exactly the annual interval it always meant. The control is operable rather than decorative: both selects are named, they sit in a GET form that carries the mode, presentation, and data selections through a submit, and the selected span is reflected in every link on the page, so a chosen span can be linked, bookmarked, and shared. The route parses the span defensively, ordering a reversed one and widening a zero-length one to the annual interval ending at that year, rather than throwing on any value the control could not have produced. Until 2026-09-21 the control was two native range inputs; the owner redefined this criterion on that date (data/owner-scope-decision-2026-09-21-explore-year-control.json). On 2026-09-20 ExploreView.tsx was moved into a three-column grid, controls left, map centre, figures right. The bound digest was refreshed for that move alone: the four modes and the four boundary overlays render exactly as this reason describes, placement is by named grid area so the document order is unchanged, and no release, clip, attribution or removal named above was touched. On 2026-09-21 ExploreYearControl.tsx and tests/browser/year-control.spec.ts were changed for the native year-select interaction described here; their evidence digests were added, and this reason still holds. On 2026-09-21 tests/explore.test.tsx moved for the whole-area boundary pick; its year-select assertions are unchanged. On 2026-09-23 ExploreView.tsx, explore.test.tsx changed for a plain-language wording pass alone; their digests were refreshed, and this reason still holds. On 2026-09-23 ExploreView.tsx and tests/explore.test.tsx changed for the owner-approved Explore layout; the two native year selects, their ranges and the GET form, which still carries mode, presentation and data, are unchanged. Their digests were refreshed, and this reason still holds.
